title: Supersonic airliner in doubt as company shifts to powering AI data centers
script:
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby doubts the Boom Overture airliner will fly by 2029.
Boom Supersonic is now shifting resources toward powering AI data centers.
This shift follows the loss of a major customer for the power division at Boom Supersonic.
The Overture jet was meant to be the first supersonic airliner in decades.
Data centers now consume massive power for AI training.
Boom Supersonic is trying to capture this surging energy demand instead of focusing on flight.
United Airlines remains cautious about the timeline for supersonic travel.
Would you trust a plane from a data center power company?

editor.one_line: Strong reporting, but visuals are repetitive and lack variety in pacing.
script_fixes: LINE 3: Replace 'a major customer' with the specific name of the client if available, or 'a key data center partner'.
LINE 6: Remove 'instead of focusing on flight' as it is editorializing; replace with 'to diversify revenue streams'.
visual_notes: line 4: The same aircraft image is reused from previous frames, creating visual fatigue.
line 5: The image of a person working on hardware is generic and lacks a direct connection to Boom
line 6: The aircraft footage is repeated again; needs a graphic or diagram of the power unit.
